claim: S. cerevisiae broadly re-configures the nutrient transporters at the plasma membrane in response to amino acid availability through endocytosis of sugar- and amino acid transporters (Müller et al., 2015).
source: Previously, we have shown that S. cerevisiae broadly re-configures the nutrient transporters at the plasma membrane in response to amino acid availability, through endocytosis of sugar- and amino acid transporters (AATs) (Müller et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Müller et al., 2015).

claim: A genome-wide screen revealed that the selective endocytosis of four AATs during starvation required the α-arrestin family protein Art2/Ecm21.
source: A genome-wide screen now revealed that the selective endocytosis of four AATs during starvation required the α-arrestin family protein Art2/Ecm21, an adaptor for the ubiquitin ligase Rsp5, and its induction through the general amino acid control pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from a genome-wide screen described in the manuscript.

claim: Art2 is an adaptor for the ubiquitin ligase Rsp5.
source: A genome-wide screen now revealed that the selective endocytosis of four AATs during starvation required the α-arrestin family protein Art2/Ecm21, an adaptor for the ubiquitin ligase Rsp5, and its induction through the general amino acid control pathway.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Art2 induction occurs through the general amino acid control pathway.
source: A genome-wide screen now revealed that the selective endocytosis of four AATs during starvation required the α-arrestin family protein Art2/Ecm21, an adaptor for the ubiquitin ligase Rsp5, and its induction through the general amino acid control pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing Art2 regulation by the GAAC pathway.

claim: Art2 uses a basic patch to recognize C-terminal acidic sorting motifs in AATs.
source: Art2 uses a basic patch to recognize C-terminal acidic sorting motifs in AATs and thereby instructs Rsp5 to ubiquitinate proximal lysine residues.
evidence: The claim is supported by mutagenesis experiments showing that the basic patch in Art2 is required for function.

claim: Art2 instructs Rsp5 to ubiquitinate proximal lysine residues in AATs.
source: Art2 uses a basic patch to recognize C-terminal acidic sorting motifs in AATs and thereby instructs Rsp5 to ubiquitinate proximal lysine residues.
evidence: The claim is supported by ubiquitination assays and mass spectrometry data.

claim: When amino acids are in excess, Rsp5 uses TORC1-activated Art1 to detect N-terminal acidic sorting motifs within the same AATs.
source: When amino acids are in excess, Rsp5 instead uses TORC1-activated Art1 to detect N-terminal acidic sorting motifs within the same AATs, which initiates exclusive substrate-induced endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to prior work on Art1-mediated endocytosis.

claim: Art1-mediated recognition of N-terminal acidic sorting motifs initiates exclusive substrate-induced endocytosis.
source: When amino acids are in excess, Rsp5 instead uses TORC1-activated Art1 to detect N-terminal acidic sorting motifs within the same AATs, which initiates exclusive substrate-induced endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing Art1-dependent endocytosis in response to substrate excess.

claim: Amino acid excess or starvation activate complementary α-arrestin-Rsp5-complexes to control selective endocytosis and adapt nutrient acquisition.
source: Thus, amino acid excess or starvation activate complementary α-arrestin-Rsp5-complexes to control selective endocytosis and adapt nutrient acquisition.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The human genome encodes more than 60 known amino acid transporters (AATs).
source: For the selective transport of amino acids across the plasma membrane (PM) and other cellular membranes, the human genome encodes more than 60 known amino acid transporters (AATs).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about the human genome.

claim: Mutations in AATs cause severe defects of amino acid metabolism.
source: Mutations in AATs cause severe defects of amino acid metabolism, and the deregulation of AATs is linked to a range of human pathologies, including neurodegenerative diseases, diabetes and cancer (Kandasamy et al., 2018; Smith, 1990; McCracken and Edinger, 2013; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Deregulation of AATs is linked to neurodegenerative diseases, diabetes and cancer.
source: Mutations in AATs cause severe defects of amino acid metabolism, and the deregulation of AATs is linked to a range of human pathologies, including neurodegenerative diseases, diabetes and cancer (Kandasamy et al., 2018; Smith, 1990; McCracken and Edinger, 2013; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: AATs belong to the family of solute carriers (SLCs).
source: AATs belong to the family of solute carriers (SLCs) and form selective pores that change from an outward- to an inward-facing conformation and thereby transport their amino acid substrates across membranes.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about AAT classification.

claim: AATs form selective pores that change from an outward- to an inward-facing conformation to transport amino acid substrates across membranes.
source: AATs belong to the family of solute carriers (SLCs) and form selective pores that change from an outward- to an inward-facing conformation and thereby transport their amino acid substrates across membranes.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about AAT mechanism.

claim: The addition of AATs to the PM or their selective removal by endocytosis determines quantity and quality of amino acid transport.
source: Hence, the addition of AATs to the PM or their selective removal by endocytosis determines quantity and quality of amino acid transport.
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the mechanism of AAT function.

claim: In human cells, the molecular mechanisms leading to the selective endocytosis of AATs are largely unclear.
source: In human cells, the molecular mechanisms leading to the selective endocytosis of AATs are largely unclear.
evidence: The claim is based on the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Yeast cells frequently experience acute fluctuations in amino acid availability (Broach, 2012).
source: Yeast cells frequently experience acute fluctuations in amino acid availability (Broach, 2012) and can rapidly remodel their 21 PM-localized AATs to optimize the import of amino acids with regard to the quantity and quality of the nitrogen source available (Grenson et al., 1966; Grenson, 1966; André, 2018; Van Belle and André, 2001; Bianchi et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Yeast cells can rapidly remodel their 21 PM-localized AATs to optimize amino acid import (Grenson et al., 1966; Grenson, 1966; André, 2018; Van Belle and André, 2001; Bianchi et al., 2019).
source: Yeast cells frequently experience acute fluctuations in amino acid availability (Broach, 2012) and can rapidly remodel their 21 PM-localized AATs to optimize the import of amino acids with regard to the quantity and quality of the nitrogen source available (Grenson et al., 1966; Grenson, 1966; André, 2018; Van Belle and André, 2001; Bianchi et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The selective, ubiquitin-dependent endocytosis of AATs and other integral PM proteins frequently requires the HECT-type ubiquitin ligase Rsp5 (Hein et al., 1995; Dupré et al., 2004; Belgareh-Touzé et al., 2008).
source: The selective, ubiquitin-dependent endocytosis of AATs and other integral PM proteins frequently requires the HECT-type ubiquitin ligase Rsp5, the orthologue of human Nedd4 (Hein et al., 1995; Dupré et al., 2004; Belgareh-Touzé et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Rsp5 is the orthologue of human Nedd4.
source: The selective, ubiquitin-dependent endocytosis of AATs and other integral PM proteins frequently requires the HECT-type ubiquitin ligase Rsp5, the orthologue of human Nedd4 (Hein et al., 1995; Dupré et al., 2004; Belgareh-Touzé et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about protein orthology.

claim: Rsp5 interacts with α-arrestin proteins to specifically recognize and ubiquitinate PM proteins (Nikko et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2008).
source: To specifically recognize and ubiquitinate PM proteins, Rsp5 interacts with the α-arrestin proteins, a family of ubiquitin ligase adaptors (Nikko et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The budding yeast genome encodes 14 α-arrestin proteins (Art1-10, Bul1-3 and Spo23).
source: The budding yeast genome encodes 14 α-arrestin proteins (arrestin-related trafficking adaptors, ARTs; Art1-10, Bul1-3 and Spo23), which function in a partially redundant manner (Becuwe et al., 2012a; MacGurn et al., 2012; Babst, 2020; O'Donnell and Schmidt, 2019; Nikko and Pelham, 2009).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about the yeast genome.

claim: Yeast α-arrestins function in a partially redundant manner (Becuwe et al., 2012a; MacGurn et al., 2012; Babst, 2020; O'Donnell and Schmidt, 2019; Nikko and Pelham, 2009).
source: The budding yeast genome encodes 14 α-arrestin proteins (arrestin-related trafficking adaptors, ARTs; Art1-10, Bul1-3 and Spo23), which function in a partially redundant manner (Becuwe et al., 2012a; MacGurn et al., 2012; Babst, 2020; O'Donnell and Schmidt, 2019; Nikko and Pelham, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Six α-arrestins have been identified in humans (Alvarez, 2008).
source: Six α-arrestins have been identified in humans (Alvarez, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: α-Arrestin proteins use PPxY (PY) motifs to interact directly with the three WW domains of Rsp5/Nedd4 (Becuwe et al., 2012a; Rauch and Martin-Serrano, 2011).
source: α-Arrestin proteins use PPxY (PY) motifs to interact directly with the three WW domains of Rsp5/Nedd4 (Becuwe et al., 2012a; Rauch and Martin-Serrano, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The arrestin domains of α-arrestins have large, disordered loop- and tail-like insertions that contribute to their function (Baile et al., 2019).
source: These domains have large, disordered loop- and tail-like insertions that contribute to the function of ARTs (Baile et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The binding of α-arrestins to Rsp5 results in their ubiquitination, which is required for function in several cases (Lin et al., 2008; Becuwe et al., 2012b; Hovsepian et al., 2017).
source: In several cases, the binding of α−arrestins to Rsp5 results in their ubiquitination, which is required for function (Lin et al., 2008; Becuwe et al., 2012b; Hovsepian et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: In case of Art1, ubiquitination determines its localization (Lin et al., 2008).
source: In case of Art1, ubiquitination determines its localization (Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Additional ubiquitination of ARTs can target them for proteasomal degradation, which is counteracted by deubiquitinating enzymes (Ho et al., 2017).
source: Additional ubiquitination of ARTs can target them for proteasomal degradation, which is counteracted by deubiquitinating enzymes (Ho et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Several α-arrestins are activated by dephosphorylation events in response to nutrient availability or other cellular stresses (Becuwe et al., 2012a; O'Donnell et al., 2013; Alvaro et al., 2014; Becuwe et al., 2012b; Becuwe and Léon, 2014; Merhi and André, 2012).
source: Several α−arrestins are activated by dephosphorylation events in response to nutrient availability or other cellular stresses (Becuwe et al., 2012a; O'Donnell et al., 2013; Alvaro et al., 2014; Becuwe et al., 2012b; Becuwe and Léon, 2014; Merhi and André, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: High levels of amino acids activate TORC1, which leads to inhibition of the kinase Npr1 and thereby promotes the activity of Art1 (MacGurn et al., 2011).
source: One example are high levels of amino acids, which activate the target of rapamycin complex 1 (TORC1). This leads to inhibition of the kinase Npr1 and thereby promotes the activity of Art1 (MacGurn et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Ppz phosphatases activate Art1 by dephosphorylation of its Npr1-dependent phosphorylation sites (Lee et al., 2019).
source: At the PM, Ppz phosphatases activate Art1 by dephosphorylation of its Npr1-dependent phosphorylation sites (Lee et al., 2019) and thereby stimulate ubiquitination and endocytosis of the Art1 cargoes Mup1 (methionine transporter), Can1 (arginine transporter), Tat2 (tyrosine and tryptophan transporter) and Lyp1 (lysine transporter) in response to substrate excess.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Ppz phosphatases stimulate ubiquitination and endocytosis of Mup1, Can1, Tat2 and Lyp1 in response to substrate excess (Lee et al., 2019).
source: At the PM, Ppz phosphatases activate Art1 by dephosphorylation of its Npr1-dependent phosphorylation sites (Lee et al., 2019) and thereby stimulate ubiquitination and endocytosis of the Art1 cargoes Mup1 (methionine transporter), Can1 (arginine transporter), Tat2 (tyrosine and tryptophan transporter) and Lyp1 (lysine transporter) in response to substrate excess.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: TORC1 signaling promotes endocytosis of Gap1 via the ARTs Bul1/2 (Merhi and André, 2012).
source: Similarly, TORC1 signaling also promotes endocytosis of the general amino acid permease (Gap1) via the ARTs Bul1/2 (Merhi and André, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The flux of methionine through Mup1 or arginine through Can1 requires conformational changes into the inward-facing conformation, which probably dislodge a C-terminal plug (Guiney et al., 2016; Gournas et al., 2018; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
source: The flux of methionine through Mup1 or arginine through Can1 requires conformational changes into the inward-facing conformation, which probably dislodge a C-terminal plug that otherwise 'seals' the pore. At the same time, it exposes an N-terminal acidic patch that is recognized by activated Art1. Art1 interacts with this acidic patch and then orients Rsp5 to ubiquitinate nearby lysine residues (Guiney et al., 2016; Gournas et al., 2018; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Conformational changes in Mup1 and Can1 expose an N-terminal acidic patch that is recognized by activated Art1 (Guiney et al., 2016; Gournas et al., 2018; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
source: The flux of methionine through Mup1 or arginine through Can1 requires conformational changes into the inward-facing conformation, which probably dislodge a C-terminal plug that otherwise 'seals' the pore. At the same time, it exposes an N-terminal acidic patch that is recognized by activated Art1. Art1 interacts with this acidic patch and then orients Rsp5 to ubiquitinate nearby lysine residues (Guiney et al., 2016; Gournas et al., 2018; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Art1 interacts with the N-terminal acidic patch and orients Rsp5 to ubiquitinate nearby lysine residues (Guiney et al., 2016; Gournas et al., 2018; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
source: The flux of methionine through Mup1 or arginine through Can1 requires conformational changes into the inward-facing conformation, which probably dislodge a C-terminal plug that otherwise 'seals' the pore. At the same time, it exposes an N-terminal acidic patch that is recognized by activated Art1. Art1 interacts with this acidic patch and then orients Rsp5 to ubiquitinate nearby lysine residues (Guiney et al., 2016; Gournas et al., 2018; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Similar results have been obtained for the uracil transporter Fur4 (Keener and Babst, 2013).
source: Similar results have been obtained for the uracil transporter Fur4 (Keener and Babst, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Stimulus-induced phosphorylation of nutrient transporters may add an additional layer of complexity (Marchal et al., 1998; Paiva et al., 2009).
source: A further layer of complexity may be added by stimulus-induced phosphorylation of nutrient transporters (Marchal et al., 1998; Paiva et al., 2009), akin to the recognition of G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) by β–arrestins in mammalian cells (Nikko et al., 2008; Nobles et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature and involves speculation about additional regulatory mechanisms.

claim: Nutrient limitation, acute starvation or rapamycin treatment can induce nutrient transporter endocytosis (Crapeau et al., 2014; Hovsepian et al., 2017; Jones et al., 2012; Laidlaw et al., 2020; Lang et al., 2014; Müller et al., 2015; Schmidt et al., 1998; Yang et al., 2020).
source: Yet, not only substrate transport can induce nutrient transporter endocytosis, but also nutrient limitation, acute starvation or rapamycin treatment (Crapeau et al., 2014; Hovsepian et al., 2017; Jones et al., 2012; Laidlaw et al., 2020; Lang et al., 2014; Müller et al., 2015; Schmidt et al., 1998; Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis is part of a coordinated catabolic cascade that maintains amino acid homeostasis (Müller et al., 2015; Jones et al., 2012).
source: Starvation-induced endocytosis is part of a coordinated catabolic cascade. Together with proteasomal degradation and with macro- and micro-autophagy, it maintains amino acid homeostasis to allow entry into quiescence for cell survival during nutrient limitation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to prior literature.

claim: The catabolic cascade at the onset of starvation appears to be conserved in metazoans (Mejlvang et al., 2018; Edinger and Thompson, 2002a; Edinger and Thompson, 2002b; Vabulas and Hartl, 2005; Suraweera et al., 2012).
source: This catabolic cascade at the onset of starvation appears to be conserved in metazoans (Mejlvang et al., 2018; Edinger and Thompson, 2002a; Edinger and Thompson, 2002b; Vabulas and Hartl, 2005; Suraweera et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: 50 GFP-tagged proteins were detected at the PM in cells growing exponentially under defined (rich) conditions, including eight different AATs and six different carbohydrate transporters.
source: In cells growing exponentially under defined (rich) conditions, we detected 50 GFP-tagged proteins at the PM, including eight different AATs and six different carbohydrate transporters (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: A fraction of PM proteins was additionally detected inside the vacuole, suggesting continuous turnover.
source: A fraction of these proteins was additionally detected inside the vacuole (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), suggesting continuous turnover.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and involves inference about protein turnover.

claim: In response to starvation, 15 different PM proteins were selectively removed and transported into the vacuole, including four AATs (Mup1, Can1, Lyp1, Tat2) and four carbohydrate transporters (Hxt1, Hxt2, Hxt3, Itr1).
source: Consistently, in response to starvation 15 (out of 50) different PM proteins were selectively removed and transported into the vacuole, including four AATs (Mup1, Can1, Lyp1, Tat2) and four carbohydrate transporters (Hxt1, Hxt2, Hxt3, Itr1) (Figure 1B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Gap1 and Mep2 were up-regulated and localized to the PM in response to starvation.
source: The general amino acid permease Gap1 and the ammonium permease Mep2 were up-regulated and now localized to the PM.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The localization of 35 GFP-tagged proteins to the PM remained largely unchanged in response to starvation.
source: The localization of 35 GFP-tagged proteins to the PM remained largely unchanged, although in some instances the vacuolar GFP fluorescence was increased (Figure 1A,B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Low levels of methionine in the growth medium did not efficiently trigger Mup1 endocytosis.
source: Low levels of methionine in the growth medium did not efficiently trigger its endocytosis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy and western blot.

claim: Above a critical methionine concentration, the vast majority of Mup1-GFP was removed from the PM by endocytosis and transported to the vacuole via the MVB pathway.
source: Yet, above a critical methionine concentration the vast majority of Mup1-GFP was removed from the PM by endocytosis and was subsequently transported to the vacuole via the multivesicular body (MVB) pathway (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy and western blot.

claim: Substrate-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was rapid and efficient: within 60–90 min after methionine addition Mup1 was almost quantitatively delivered to the vacuole.
source: Substrate-induced endocytosis was rapid and efficient: within 60–90 min after methionine addition Mup1 was almost quantitatively delivered to the vacuole.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy and western blot.

claim: Excess methionine appeared to exclusively induce endocytosis of Mup1 since all other tested PM proteins remained at the cell surface.
source: Excess methionine appeared to exclusively induce endocytosis of Mup1 since all other tested PM proteins remained at the cell surface (Figure 1A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The exclusive substrate-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was dependent on its methionine transport activity as shown by using the Mup1-G78N mutant (Busto et al., 2018).
source: This exclusive substrate-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was also dependent on its methionine transport activity as shown by using the Mup1-G78N mutant, which cannot transition to the open-inward conformation (Busto et al., 2018; Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to prior literature.

claim: The high-affinity AATs Mup1, Can1, Tat2 and Lyp1 undergo exclusive endocytic down-regulation in response to excess of their respective substrates but remained stable at the PM when the substrate of another permease was present in excess (Gournas et al., 2017; Busto et al., 2018; Nikko and Pelham, 2009).
source: These results are consistent with earlier reports showing that the high-affinity AATs Mup1, Can1, Tat2 and Lyp1 undergo exclusive endocytic down-regulation in response to excess of their respective substrates but remained stable at the PM when the substrate of another permease was present in excess (Gournas et al., 2017; Busto et al., 2018; Nikko and Pelham, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature and is consistent with the experimental data.

claim: The starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was independent of its capability to transport its substrate.
source: In contrast, the starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was independent of its capability to transport its substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) and was also observed upon starvation for individual essential amino acids (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was observed upon starvation for individual essential amino acids.
source: In contrast, the starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was independent of its capability to transport its substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) and was also observed upon starvation for individual essential amino acids (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: In response to starvation, a broad range of nutrient transporters were selectively removed from the PM by endocytosis and transported into the vacuole within 3–6 hr.
source: Hence, in response to starvation, a broad range of nutrient transporters, including four AATs (Mup1, Can1, Lyp1, Tat2) and four carbohydrate transporters (Hxt1, Hxt2, Hxt3, Itr1) as well as other membrane proteins, were selectively removed from the PM by endocytosis and transported into the vacuole within 3–6 hr.
evidence: The claim is a summary of experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Substrate-induced endocytosis of AATs was quick and exclusive.
source: In contrast, substrate-induced endocytosis of AATs was quick and exclusive (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Substrate-induced endocytosis of Mup1, Can1 and Lyp1 required TORC1 signaling to allow ubiquitination by Rsp5 in complex with Art1 (Lin et al., 2008; Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018; Gournas et al., 2018; MacGurn et al., 2011).
source: Earlier work showed that substrate-induced endocytosis of the AATs Mup1, Can1 and Lyp1 required TORC1 signaling to allow ubiquitination of the transporters by the HECT-type ubiquitin ligase Rsp5 in complex with the α-arrestin Art1 (Lin et al., 2008; Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018; Gournas et al., 2018; MacGurn et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Mup1-pHluorin is a suitable reporter to identify mutants that block trafficking of Mup1 from the PM into the vacuole.
source: Hence Mup1-pHluorin is a suitable reporter to identify mutants that block trafficking of Mup1 from the PM into the vacuole.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that Mup1-pHluorin fluorescence is quenched in vacuoles of WT cells but not in ESCRT mutants.

claim: 128 mutants exhibited Mup1-pHluorin fluorescence after starvation in the genome-wide screen.
source: The vast majority of mutants efficiently quenched the fluorescence of Mup1-pHluorin after starvation, but 128 mutants still exhibited Mup1-pHluorin fluorescence after starvation (Figure 2C, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the flow cytometry screen.

claim: Class one mutants retained Mup1-pHluorin at the PM after starvation (105 mutants).
source: Class one mutants retained Mup1-pHluorin at the PM after starvation (105 mutants, e.g. apm2Δ mutants).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: In class two mutants, Mup1-pHluorin was detected on small intracellular objects (seven mutants).
source: In class two mutants, Mup1-pHluorin was detected on small intracellular objects (seven mutants, e.g. vam3Δ mutants).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Class three mutants accumulated Mup1-pHluorin in larger class E compartment-like objects (15 mutants).
source: Class three mutants accumulated Mup1-pHluorin in larger class E compartment-like objects (15 mutants, e.g. vps4Δ mutants).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: One Class four mutant (pep4Δ) did not efficiently quench Mup1-pHluorin fluorescence inside the vacuole because it is deficient in the main lysosomal protease.
source: One Class four mutant (pep4Δ) did not efficiently quench Mup1-pHluorin fluorescence inside the vacuole, as it is deficient in the main lysosomal protease.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and established knowledge about pep4Δ mutants.

claim: The screen identified major general regulators of endosomal transport and was enriched for proteins annotated as components of the PM, endosomes and vacuoles.
source: Gene ontology (GO) analysis confirmed that our screen identified major general regulators of endosomal transport (e.g. the ESCRT complexes) and was enriched for proteins that are annotated as components of the PM, endosomes and vacuoles (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3) suggesting that it was successful.
evidence: The claim is supported by GO analysis of the screen results.

claim: 100 of the class one mutants were specifically required for starvation-induced endocytosis but not for methionine-induced endocytosis.
source: However, the majority (100) of the class one mutants (Mup1-pHluorin retained at the PM) was specifically required for starvation-induced endocytosis but not for methionine-induced endocytosis (Figure 2D, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy comparing starvation and methionine treatment.

claim: Among the 14 α-arrestins encoded by the yeast genome, the screen identified only Ecm21/Art2 to be specifically required for starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1.
source: Among the 14 α−arrestins encoded by the yeast genome, our screen identified only Ecm21/Art2 to be specifically required for starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the genome-wide screen.

claim: Efficient methionine-induced endocytosis of Mup1 required Art1 but not Art2.
source: Efficient methionine-induced endocytosis of Mup1 required Art1 but not Art2 (Figure 3A), consistent with earlier observations (Guiney et al., 2016; MacGurn et al., 2011; Busto et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to prior literature.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was slower than methionine-induced endocytosis.
source: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was slower than methionine-induced endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing the kinetics of the two processes.

claim: In WT cells, 240–360 min after onset of starvation the majority of Mup1-GFP was removed from the PM and sorted into vacuoles for degradation.
source: In WT cells, 240–360 min after onset of starvation the majority of Mup1-GFP was removed from the PM and sorted into vacuoles for degradation (Figure 3A,B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy and western blot.

claim: In art2Δ mutants, but not in art1Δ mutants, the vast majority of Mup1-GFP remained at the PM and was no longer delivered to vacuoles during starvation.
source: In art2Δ mutants, but not in art1Δ mutants, the vast majority of Mup1-GFP remained at the PM and was no longer delivered to vacuoles (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Re-expression of Art1 or Art2 in the corresponding mutants restored methionine- or starvation-induced Mup1 endocytosis, respectively.
source: Re-expression of Art1 or Art2 in the corresponding mutants restored methionine- or starvation-induced Mup1 endocytosis, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from complementation experiments.

claim: Art2 was required for the efficient starvation-induced endocytosis of all four AATs: Mup1, Can1, Lyp1, and Tat2.
source: Importantly, Art2 was required for the efficient starvation-induced endocytosis of all four AATs, Mup1, Can1, Lyp1, and Tat2 (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The same four AATs (Mup1, Can1, Lyp1 and Tat2) depend on Art1 for efficient substrate-induced endocytosis (Gournas et al., 2017; MacGurn et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2008; Nikko and Pelham, 2009).
source: Interestingly, the same four AATs (Mup1, Can1, Lyp1 and Tat2) also depend on Art1 for efficient substrate-induced endocytosis (Gournas et al., 2017; MacGurn et al., 2011; Lin et al., 2008; Nikko and Pelham, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Ina1 was dependent on Art2.
source: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Ina1 was also dependent on Art2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), while other PM proteins (e.g. the uracil transporter Fur4 or the hexose transporters Hxt1 and Hxt2) were largely independent of Art2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Other PM proteins (e.g. Fur4, Hxt1 and Hxt2) were largely independent of Art2 for starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Ina1 was also dependent on Art2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), while other PM proteins (e.g. the uracil transporter Fur4 or the hexose transporters Hxt1 and Hxt2) were largely independent of Art2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Art1 protein levels were unchanged in response to starvation.
source: WB analysis of total cell lysates indicated that 6xHis-TEV-3xFlag-tagged Art1 protein levels were unchanged in response to starvation (Figure 4A, lanes 2,3), whereas the protein levels of the functional 170kD protein Art2-HTF (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) were up-regulated in response to starvation (Figure 4A, lanes 5,6; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from western blot analysis.

claim: Art2 protein levels were up-regulated in response to starvation.
source: WB analysis of total cell lysates indicated that 6xHis-TEV-3xFlag-tagged Art1 protein levels were unchanged in response to starvation (Figure 4A, lanes 2,3), whereas the protein levels of the functional 170kD protein Art2-HTF (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) were up-regulated in response to starvation (Figure 4A, lanes 5,6; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from western blot analysis.

claim: ART2 mRNA levels increased during starvation.
source: Quantitative reverse transcription (RT) PCR analysis indicated that also the ART2 mRNA levels increased during starvation (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RT-qPCR analysis.

claim: Disrupting the GAAC pathway (gcn4Δ) eliminated the induction of Art2 in response to starvation at mRNA and protein levels.
source: Disrupting the GAAC pathway (gcn4∆) eliminated the induction of Art2 in response to starvation at mRNA and protein levels (Figure 4B,C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from RT-qPCR and western blot analysis.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1-GFP was hampered in gcn4Δ cells and several other gcn mutants.
source: Consistently, the starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1-GFP was hampered in gcn4∆ cells and several other gcn mutants (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Can1 was dependent on the GAAC pathway.
source: Also, starvation-induced endocytosis of Can1 was dependent on the GAAC pathway (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Mutations in the predicted Gcn4-binding sites in the ART2 promoter prevented Art2 protein level increase in response to starvation and impaired starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1-GFP.
source: When we introduced mutations in the predicted Gcn4-binding sites in the ART2 promoter, Art2 protein levels no longer increased in response to starvation, and starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1-GFP was impaired (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from western blot and fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The ART2 promoter induced the expression of Art1 during starvation when used to replace the ART1 promoter.
source: When the ART2 promoter region was used to replace the ART1 promoter, it also induced the expression of Art1 during starvation (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from western blot analysis.

claim: The upregulation of Art1 protein levels driven by the ART2 promoter failed to restore starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1-GFP in art2Δ cells.
source: Yet, the upregulation of Art1 protein levels driven by the ART2 promoter failed to restore starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1-GFP in art2∆ cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The expression of a constitutively translated Gcn4C construct increased Art2 protein levels already under rich conditions.
source: The expression of a constitutively translated Gcn4C construct (Mueller and Hinnebusch, 1986) increased Art2 protein levels already under rich conditions, as revealed by WB analysis (Figure 4F, compare Art2 protein levels in lanes 1 and 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 1G), and drove unscheduled Mup1-GFP endocytosis (Figure 4F, lower panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from western blot and fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Over-expression of Art2 using the TDH3 promoter initiated Mup1-GFP endocytosis already under nutrient replete conditions and bypassed the requirement of Gcn4 during starvation.
source: Consistently, over-expression of Art2 in WT cells or in gcn4∆ mutants using the strong and constitutively active TDH3 promoter (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C) initiated Mup1-GFP endocytosis already under nutrient replete conditions (Figure 4G) and bypassed the requirement of Gcn4 during starvation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: During amino acid starvation, Art2 transcription was induced via the GAAC pathway, leading to the up-regulation of Art2 protein levels.
source: These results indicated that during amino acid starvation, Art2 transcription was induced via the GAAC pathway, leading to the up-regulation of Art2 protein levels.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion supported by the experimental data.

claim: The up-regulation of Art2 protein levels was sufficient to drive Mup1 endocytosis.
source: Moreover, it seemed that the up-regulation of Art2 protein levels was sufficient to drive Mup1 endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that Art2 overexpression drives endocytosis.

claim: Under amino acid replete conditions Art2 must be tightly repressed to prevent AAT endocytosis.
source: Hence, under amino acid replete conditions Art2 must be tightly repressed to prevent AAT endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observation that Art2 overexpression drives endocytosis under rich conditions.

claim: A pool of Mup1 was ubiquitinated prior to the onset of starvation.
source: This analysis indicated that a pool of Mup1 was ubiquitinated prior to the onset of starvation (Figure 5A, lane 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: At the onset of starvation, ubiquitination of Mup1-GFP appeared to decrease for some time.
source: At the onset of starvation, ubiquitination of Mup1-GFP appeared to decrease for some time (Figure 5A lanes 2–4), until ubiquitination of Mup1-GFP began to increase again after 2–3 hr during starvation (Figure 5A lanes 4–6), temporally coinciding with Art2 induction and starvation-induced endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: Ubiquitination of Mup1-GFP began to increase again after 2–3 hr during starvation, temporally coinciding with Art2 induction and starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: At the onset of starvation, ubiquitination of Mup1-GFP appeared to decrease for some time (Figure 5A lanes 2–4), until ubiquitination of Mup1-GFP began to increase again after 2–3 hr during starvation (Figure 5A lanes 4–6), temporally coinciding with Art2 induction and starvation-induced endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: In art2Δ cells, the increase of ubiquitination during starvation was no longer observed.
source: Mup1-GFP was still ubiquitinated in art2Δ cells growing under rich conditions (Figure 5B lane 4) and seemingly de-ubiquitinated at the onset of starvation, but the increase of ubiquitination during starvation was no longer observed (Figure 5B, lane 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: Art2 was essential for the starvation-induced ubiquitination of Mup1.
source: Hence, Art2 was essential for the starvation-induced ubiquitination of Mup1.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data showing loss of ubiquitination in art2Δ mutants.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 was particularly dependent on the WW3 domain of Rsp5.
source: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 (but not methionine-induced endocytosis) was particularly dependent on the WW3 domain of Rsp5 (Figure 5C,D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy using Rsp5 WW domain mutants.

claim: Mutations in the PY motif within the predicted arrestin fold of Art2 (P748,P749,Y750) reduced starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1-GFP.
source: Mutations in the PY motif that resides within the predicted arrestin fold of Art2 (P748,P749,Y750) reduced starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1-GFP (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Interaction between WW3 in Rsp5 and the PY motif (748-750) of Art2 was required for the efficient starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1.
source: We suggest that interaction between WW3 in Rsp5 and the PY motif (748-750) of Art2 was required for the efficient starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data showing the requirement of both WW3 and the PY motif.

claim: Two N-terminal lysine residues (K16 and K27) and two C-terminal lysine residues (K567 and K572) in Mup1 were found to be ubiquitinated by LC-MS.
source: Two N-terminal lysine residues (K16 and K27) and two C-terminal lysine residues (K567 and K572) in Mup1 were found to be ubiquitinated (Figure 5F. Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), consistent with available high-throughput proteomic datasets (Swaney et al., 2013; Iesmantavicius et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry and citations to prior proteomic studies.

claim: Two N-terminal lysine residues (K27, K28) in Mup1 were ubiquitinated by Art1-Rsp5 and required for methionine-induced endocytosis (Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
source: Earlier reports showed that two N-terminal lysine residues (K27, K28) in Mup1 were ubiquitinated by Art1-Rsp5 and required for methionine-induced endocytosis (Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014; Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Preventing the ubiquitination of the C-terminal lysine residues (K567,572R) abrogated starvation-induced ubiquitination of Mup1.
source: Preventing the ubiquitination of the C-terminal lysine residues (K567,572R) abrogated starvation-induced ubiquitination of Mup1 (Figure 5G, lanes 7–9), whereas Mup1K27,28R-GFP was still ubiquitinated after starvation (Figure 5G, lanes 4–6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: Mup1K27,28R-GFP was still ubiquitinated after starvation.
source: Preventing the ubiquitination of the C-terminal lysine residues (K567,572R) abrogated starvation-induced ubiquitination of Mup1 (Figure 5G, lanes 7–9), whereas Mup1K27,28R-GFP was still ubiquitinated after starvation (Figure 5G, lanes 4–6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: Upon methionine treatment, Mup1K567,572R-GFP ubiquitination was comparable to WT Mup1.
source: Upon methionine treatment, Mup1K567,572R-GFP ubiquitination was comparable to WT Mup1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, lanes 1–4), while the ubiquitination of Mup1K27,28R was impaired as reported previously (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, lanes 5,6) (Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: The ubiquitination of Mup1K27,28R was impaired upon methionine treatment (Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
source: Upon methionine treatment, Mup1K567,572R-GFP ubiquitination was comparable to WT Mup1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, lanes 1–4), while the ubiquitination of Mup1K27,28R was impaired as reported previously (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, lanes 5,6) (Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018; Ghaddar et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and citations to prior literature.

claim: The quadruple mutant Mup1K27,28,567,572R-GFP appeared to be devoid of ubiquitination.
source: The quadruple mutant Mup1K27,28,567,572R-GFP always appeared to be devoid of ubiquitination (Figure 5G, lanes 11,12; Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, lanes 7,8), suggesting that the two N-terminal and the two C-terminal lysine residues are the major sites for ubiquitination.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: The two N-terminal and the two C-terminal lysine residues are the major sites for ubiquitination in Mup1.
source: The quadruple mutant Mup1K27,28,567,572R-GFP always appeared to be devoid of ubiquitination (Figure 5G, lanes 11,12; Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, lanes 7,8), suggesting that the two N-terminal and the two C-terminal lysine residues are the major sites for ubiquitination.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and involves inference from the quadruple mutant phenotype.

claim: The quadruple lysine mutation rendered Mup1K27,28,567,572R-GFP refractory to methionine- and starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: Consistently, the quadruple lysine mutation rendered Mup1K27,28,567,572R-GFP refractory to methionine- and starvation-induced endocytosis (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Mutations in the N-terminal lysine residues (K27,28R) blocked methionine-induced endocytosis, but not starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: Mutations in the N-terminal lysine residues (K27,28R) blocked methionine-induced endocytosis, but not starvation-induced endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1K567,572R-GFP was specifically blocked, but not its methionine-induced endocytosis.
source: In contrast, starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1K567,572R-GFP was specifically blocked, but not its methionine-induced endocytosis (Figure 5H).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Art2 directs Rsp5 to the ubiquitination of the C-terminal lysine residues K567 and K572 during starvation.
source: Collectively, these results suggested that Art2 directs Rsp5 to the ubiquitination of the C-terminal lysine residues K567 and K572 during starvation, whereas Art1-Rsp5 complexes ubiquitinated Mup1 on the two N-terminal lysine residues K27 and K28 in response to methionine excess (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data from ubiquitination assays and mutant analysis.

claim: Art1-Rsp5 complexes ubiquitinated Mup1 on the two N-terminal lysine residues K27 and K28 in response to methionine excess.
source: Collectively, these results suggested that Art2 directs Rsp5 to the ubiquitination of the C-terminal lysine residues K567 and K572 during starvation, whereas Art1-Rsp5 complexes ubiquitinated Mup1 on the two N-terminal lysine residues K27 and K28 in response to methionine excess (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data and prior literature.

claim: Mass-spectrometry analysis of immunoprecipitated Mup1-GFP from starved cells identified potential phosphorylation sites at the N-terminus (S9,23,31,42 and T34) and at the C-terminus of Mup1 (T552 and S568,573).
source: In addition to ubiquitination, our mass-spectrometry analysis of immunoprecipitated Mup1-GFP from starved cells identified potential phosphorylation sites at the N-terminus (S9,23,31,42 and T34) and at the C-terminus of Mup1 (T552 and S568,573) (Figure 6A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry.

claim: Additional phosphorylation on T560 was reported in other studies (Swaney et al., 2013; Iesmantavicius et al., 2014).
source: Additional phosphorylation on T560 was reported in other studies (Swaney et al., 2013; Iesmantavicius et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior proteomic studies.

claim: The C-terminal phosphorylation sites were proximal (T552, T560) or directly adjacent (S568, S573) to lysine residues K567 and K572 that were ubiquitinated in an Art2-dependent manner in response to starvation.
source: Of note, the C-terminal phosphorylation sites were proximal (T552, T560) or directly adjacent (S568, S573) to lysine residues K567 and K572 that were ubiquitinated in an Art2-dependent manner in response to starvation (Figure 6A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mass spectrometry and ubiquitination assays.

claim: Mutation of the C-terminal threonine residues to alanine (T552,560A) specifically blocked starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1T552,560A-GFP, but not methionine-induced endocytosis.
source: Mutation of the C-terminal threonine residues to alanine (T552,560A) to prevent phosphorylation specifically blocked starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1T552,560A-GFP, but not methionine-induced endocytosis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Mutation of T552,560A also prevented ubiquitination of Mup1 during starvation.
source: Mutation of these phosphorylation sites also prevented ubiquitination of Mup1 during starvation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: Blocking the phosphorylation of S568 and S573 impaired starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1S568,573A-GFP.
source: Blocking the phosphorylation of S568 and S573 also impaired starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1S568,573A-GFP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), yet starvation-induced ubiquitination could still be detected (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Starvation-induced ubiquitination could still be detected in Mup1S568,573A-GFP.
source: Blocking the phosphorylation of S568 and S573 also impaired starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1S568,573A-GFP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E), yet starvation-induced ubiquitination could still be detected (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: Mutation of most N-terminal serine and threonine residues to alanine (T6,25,26,34A,S9,22,23,24,31,33,42A) did not affect starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1.
source: Mutation of most N-terminal serine and threonine residues, including all experimentally determined phosphorylation sites, to alanine (T6,25,26,34A,S9,22,23,24,31,33,42A) did not affect starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The phosphorylation of C-terminal threonine residues (T552, 560) contributed to the starvation-induced Art2-Rsp5 ubiquitination of Mup1.
source: It seemed that the phosphorylation of C-terminal threonine residues (T552, 560) contributed to the starvation-induced Art2-Rsp5 ubiquitination of Mup1 and thus might add an additional layer of regulation, similar to the recognition of GPCRs by β–arrestins in mammalian cells (Shukla et al., 2014; Nikko et al., 2008; Marchal et al., 2000; Hicke et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data and involves speculation about regulatory mechanisms.

claim: An extended acidic Art1 sorting motif at the N-terminus of Mup1 is required for ubiquitination of K27,28 and subsequent Mup1 endocytosis in response to methionine excess (Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018).
source: An extended acidic Art1 sorting motif at the N-terminus of Mup1 is required for ubiquitination of K27,28 and subsequent Mup1 endocytosis in response to methionine excess (Guiney et al., 2016; Busto et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Mutations in the acidic N-terminal Art1 sorting motif of Mup1 (D43A,G47A,Q49A,T52A,L54A) blocked Art1-Rsp5-dependent methionine-induced endocytosis, but not Art2-Rsp5-dependent starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: Consistent with our model involving two distinct mechanisms for Mup1 endocytosis, mutations in the acidic N-terminal Art1 sorting motif of Mup1 (D43A,G47A,Q49A,T52A,L54A) blocked Art1-Rsp5-dependent methionine-induced endocytosis, but not Art2-Rsp5-dependent starvation-induced endocytosis (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The C-terminus of Mup1 contains an acidic patch (D549-D555), close to the ubiquitination sites K567 and K572 and the C-terminal threonine phosphorylation sites (T552, 560) involved in starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: The C-terminus of Mup1 also contains an acidic patch (D549-D555), close to the ubiquitination sites K567 and K572 and the C-terminal threonine phosphorylation sites (T552, 560) involved in starvation-induced endocytosis (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis and experimental data.

claim: Mutation of the acidic residues in the C-terminal region to basic amino acids (Mup1D549R,D551R,E554R,D555R) demonstrated that this C-terminal acidic region was specifically required for starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: Mutation of the acidic residues in this region to basic amino acids (R) demonstrated that this C-terminal acidic region was specifically required for starvation-induced endocytosis. Live cell fluorescence microscopy revealed that Mup1D549R,D551R,E554R,D555R-GFP remained at the PM in response to starvation, whereas methionine-induced endocytosis was not impaired (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Mup1D549R,D551R,E554R,D555R-GFP remained at the PM in response to starvation, whereas methionine-induced endocytosis was not impaired.
source: Mutation of the acidic residues in this region to basic amino acids (R) demonstrated that this C-terminal acidic region was specifically required for starvation-induced endocytosis. Live cell fluorescence microscopy revealed that Mup1D549R,D551R,E554R,D555R-GFP remained at the PM in response to starvation, whereas methionine-induced endocytosis was not impaired (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Art2 overexpression failed to induce endocytosis during exponential growth or starvation when the C-terminal acidic patch in Mup1 was mutated.
source: Even Art2 overexpression failed to induce endocytosis during exponential growth or starvation when the C-terminal acidic patch in Mup1 was mutated (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Mup1D549R,D551R,E554R,D555R-GFP was no longer efficiently ubiquitinated.
source: Moreover, immunoprecipitation of Mup1D549R,D551R,E554R,D555R-GFP and subsequent SDS-PAGE and WB analysis revealed that it was no longer efficiently ubiquitinated (Figure 6C, lanes 4–6), suggesting that the C-terminal acidic patch was essential for the Art2-Rsp5-dependent ubiquitination during starvation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from immunoprecipitation and western blot.

claim: The C-terminal acidic patch was essential for the Art2-Rsp5-dependent ubiquitination during starvation.
source: Moreover, immunoprecipitation of Mup1D549R,D551R,E554R,D555R-GFP and subsequent SDS-PAGE and WB analysis revealed that it was no longer efficiently ubiquitinated (Figure 6C, lanes 4–6), suggesting that the C-terminal acidic patch was essential for the Art2-Rsp5-dependent ubiquitination during starvation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data from ubiquitination assays.

claim: Comparing the amino acid sequences of the C-terminal tails of the four Art2-dependent AATs (Mup1, Can1, Tat2 and Lyp1) and of Ina1 indicated similar acidic patches.
source: Comparing the amino acid sequences of the C-terminal tails of the four Art2-dependent AATs (Mup1, Can1, Tat2 and Lyp1) and of Ina1 indicated similar acidic patches (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The Art2-dependent starvation-induced down-regulation of Can1D567R,E569R,E574R,D575R-GFP was impaired.
source: To analyze if the acidic patch in Can1 also contributed to starvation-induced endocytosis, we mutated D567, E569, E574 and E575 to arginine. Mutant Can1D567R,E569R,E574R,D575R-GFP mostly localized to the PM under growing conditions. Importantly, the Art2-dependent starvation-induced down-regulation of Can1D567R,E569R,E574R,D575R-GFP was impaired (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Mup1, Can1 and potentially also Lyp1, Tat2 and Ina1 have acidic amino acid sequences at their C-termini that could serve as sorting signal for Art2-mediated starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: These results imply that Mup1, Can1 and potentially also Lyp1, Tat2 and Ina1 have acidic amino acid sequences at their C-termini that could serve as sorting signal for Art2-mediated starvation-induced endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on sequence analysis and experimental data, with speculation about Lyp1, Tat2 and Ina1.

claim: The last 26 amino acid residues (aa 549–574) of Mup1 harbor three features that are collectively required specifically for starvation-induced endocytosis: putative phosphorylation sites, the acidic patch and the ubiquitination sites.
source: It seemed that the last 26 amino acid residues (aa 549–574) of Mup1 harbor three features that are collectively required specifically for starvation-induced endocytosis: putative phosphorylation sites, the acidic patch and the ubiquitination sites.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data from mutant analysis.

claim: Starvation-induced endocytosis of Hxt3-GFP was independent of Art2, but instead required Art4.
source: Live cell fluorescence microscopy and WB analysis showed that starvation-induced endocytosis of Hxt3-GFP was independent of Art2, but instead required Art4 (Figure 6E, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy and western blot.

claim: In art4Δ mutants, but not in art2Δ mutants, Hxt3-GFP remained mostly at the PM in response to starvation.
source: In art4∆ mutants, but not in art2Δ mutants, Hxt3-GFP remained mostly at the PM (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A) in response to starvation, and its vacuolar degradation was impaired (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B, lane 4, Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy and western blot.

claim: When the C-terminal 30 amino acids of Mup1 (aa 545–574) were fused onto the C-terminus of Hxt3, they restored starvation-induced endocytosis in art4Δ mutants.
source: However, when the C-terminal 30 amino acids of Mup1 (aa 545–574) were fused onto the C-terminus of Hxt3 (Figure 6E), they restored starvation-induced endocytosis in art4∆ mutants. This Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP chimera was now efficiently removed from the PM and transported to the vacuole in the vast majority of art4∆ cells (86%, n = 76 cells) (Figure 6E), most likely because it became an Art2 substrate.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP chimera became an Art2 substrate.
source: However, when the C-terminal 30 amino acids of Mup1 (aa 545–574) were fused onto the C-terminus of Hxt3 (Figure 6E), they restored starvation-induced endocytosis in art4∆ mutants. This Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP chimera was now efficiently removed from the PM and transported to the vacuole in the vast majority of art4∆ cells (86%, n = 76 cells) (Figure 6E), most likely because it became an Art2 substrate.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and involves inference about the mechanism.

claim: The additional deletion of ART2 (art2Δ art4Δ) blocked starvation-induced endocytosis of Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP.
source: Indeed, the additional deletion of ART2 (art2∆ art4∆) blocked starvation-induced endocytosis and demonstrated that Art2 now mediated the degradation of Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP in art4∆ mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Art2 mediated the degradation of Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP in art4Δ mutants.
source: Indeed, the additional deletion of ART2 (art2∆ art4∆) blocked starvation-induced endocytosis and demonstrated that Art2 now mediated the degradation of Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP in art4∆ mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy and western blot.

claim: The Art2-dependent endocytosis of the Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP chimera required two key features provided by the C-terminus of Mup1 (the acidic patch and the two C-terminal lysine residues).
source: The Art2-dependent endocytosis of the Hxt3-Mup1-C-GFP chimera required two key features provided by the C-terminus of Mup1 (the acidic patch and the two C-terminal lysine residues), since in art4∆ cells starvation-induced endocytosis of Hxt3-Mup1-CK567,572R-GFP and Hxt3-Mup1-CD549R,D551R,E554R,D555R-GFP was blocked (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy using chimeric constructs with mutations.

claim: The C-terminus of Mup1 (aa 545–574) encodes a portable acidic sorting signal that can be recognized by Art2 and directs Rsp5 to ubiquitinate specifically two proximal lysine residues to promote starvation-induced endocytosis.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that the C-terminus of Mup1 (aa 545–574) encodes a portable acidic sorting signal that can be recognized by Art2 and directs Rsp5 to ubiquitinate specifically two proximal lysine residues to promote starvation-induced endocytosis.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on experimental data from chimeric constructs and mutant analysis.

claim: Art2 contains a stretch of positively charged residues within the arrestin-C domain.
source: After having defined that the C-terminus of Mup1 (and possibly also the C-terminus of further Art2-targets) provides a degron sequence for Art2-Rsp5 complexes, we addressed how it could be recognized. Upon inspection of the predicted arrestin domain in Art2, we noted a stretch of positively charged residues within the arrestin-C domain (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis.

claim: Converting the basic residues in Art2 into an acidic patch (Art2K664D,R665D,R666D,K667D) abolished starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1.
source: Converting these basic residues into an acidic patch (Art2K664D,R665D,R666D,K667D) abolished starvation-induced endocytosis of Mup1 (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The Art2 basic patch mutant was expressed at similar levels as WT Art2 and was also upregulated after 3 hr of starvation.
source: Western blot analysis of total cell lysates showed that the Art2 basic patch mutant protein was expressed at similar levels as WT Art2 and was also upregulated after 3 hr of starvation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, lane 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from western blot analysis.

claim: The Art2 basic patch mutant impaired, at least partially, starvation-induced endocytosis of Can1, Lyp1 and Ina1.
source: In addition, the Art2 basic patch mutant also impaired, at least partially, starvation-induced endocytosis of Can1, Lyp1 and Ina1, while the endocytosis of Tat2 was independent of the basic patch (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: The endocytosis of Tat2 was independent of the Art2 basic patch.
source: In addition, the Art2 basic patch mutant also impaired, at least partially, starvation-induced endocytosis of Can1, Lyp1 and Ina1, while the endocytosis of Tat2 was independent of the basic patch (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from fluorescence microscopy.

claim: Art2 employed a positively charged region in its arrestin fold to recognize C-terminal acidic patches in at least three different AATs (Mup1, Can1, Lyp1) and thus mediate their endocytosis in starvation conditions.
source: Overall, it seemed that Art2 employed a positively charged region in its arrestin fold to recognize C-terminal acidic patches in at least three different AATs (Mup1, Can1, Lyp1) and thus mediate their endocytosis in starvation conditions.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on experimental data from mutant analysis.

claim: TORC1 signaling and the GAAC pathway toggle Art1- or Art2-Rsp5 complex activities to induce endocytosis of the same set of four different AATs depending on amino acid availability.
source: We find that TORC1 signaling and the general amino acid control (GAAC) pathway toggle Art1- or Art2-Rsp5 complex activities to induce endocytosis of the same set of four different AATs depending on amino acid availability.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion of the main findings supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Activated Art1- or Art2-Rsp5 complexes recognize distinct acidic sorting signals in the N-terminal (Art1 sorting signal) or C-terminal (Art2 sorting signal) regions to initiate Rsp5-dependent ubiquitination and subsequent endocytic down-regulation.
source: In these AATs, activated Art1- or Art2-Rsp5 complexes recognize distinct acidic sorting signals in the N-terminal (Art1 sorting signal) or C-terminal (Art2 sorting signal) regions to initiate Rsp5-dependent ubiquitination and subsequent endocytic down-regulation.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion of the main findings supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Using complementary α-arrestin switches in combination with distinct acidic sorting motifs in a single nutrient transporter could represent a more general mechanism to adjust transport across cellular membranes and thereby to meet metabolic demands.
source: Using such complementary α−arrestin switches in combination with distinct acidic sorting motifs in a single nutrient transporter could represent a more general mechanism to adjust transport across cellular membranes and thereby to meet metabolic demands.
evidence: The claim involves speculation about the generality of the mechanism based on the experimental findings.
